speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a young patient presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To help me understand your condition better, can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if the pain is localized or spreading?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Septic Arthritis (Left Wrist) likely due to *Mycoplasma* or viral etiology, with possible history of Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's syndrome) given the antecedent knee pain. The combination of recent camping, skin lesions, sexually active status, and a preceding monoarticular knee infection suggests a disseminated process or a reactive phenomenon. Immediate joint aspiration and blood cultures are required to rule out bacterial septic arthritis.
